prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which established the principle behind incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on B022 naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 did not weaken the scientific case, and the agreement among all six of us is not what carries it. The discovery is specific and sequential: proglucagon processing and human incretin physiology, identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form, and the biology of proglucagon-derived peptides, followed by large independent outcome trials in glycaemia, body weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease. It has changed a field in a way that is plain today, so maturity is not in question. I also think a one-part prize is the better judgment than adding a second achievement. A second part would force B022 below three names, and that would make the attribution problem I describe below worse rather than better.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point and round 1 did not resolve it. Habener is outside the credited names, Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, and the three-name cap excludes Knudsen, whose work on half-life extension is the reason weekly drugs exist. Several colleagues call this a cost, and I agree it is real and not a technicality. A physiology-centred citation is defensible only if it says plainly what it honours, and the committee should record that drug development is not being recognised by this prize. I have not been able to verify priority dates from the material available at this stage, so I treat the Mojsov question as a judgment under uncertainty and not as a settled fact.

responses.point: The chair names B050 as the cleaner two-person fallback if the GLP-1 allocation is judged too contested, and asks in the summary whether a second part should be considered.
responses.response: I take the fallback seriously but I do not think the GLP-1 allocation is contested enough to trigger it. The dispute is about who sits beside Holst and Drucker and whether Knudsen is excluded. It does not concern whether the discovery happened or whether it is mature. A weaker allocation on the strongest candidate is still better than a prize built on a clean pair whose medical consequence is indirect, as El Manira and Wahren-Herlenius point out. I keep B050 as an alternative because Mori and Walter have the cleanest credit on the list, and I accept your point that the pathway bears on diabetes and secretory biology. I would not place it above a candidate with demonstrated patient benefit.

responses.point: Marie says leaving out Mojsov would be harder to defend than leaving out an industrial developer, because identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is what made the peptide a drug target.
responses.response: This moves me. In round 1 I described Mojsov's place as resting on a disputed priority question. I now think that framing gave too much weight to the dispute. Whatever the verdict on priority, the active form is the step that connects the physiology to therapeutic design, and a citation that names it needs her. I still cannot judge the priority record from our file, and Habener's role is not addressed by the credited names. I therefore keep my uncertainty about the allocation, but I no longer see it as a reason to consider substituting another person for her.

responses.point: Rickard keeps CAR-T slightly ahead of the UPR as the first alternative, giving more weight to proven patient benefit, and says June and Sadelain is the cleaner version of B003.
responses.response: I agree on the order and on the two-name version, and I keep B003 as my first alternative. I would not turn it into a second part this year. The first-generation chimeric receptor concept sits outside the credited names, and a June and Sadelain citation has to be written carefully to be fair to that earlier work. Together with the cap, the second part would also make us cut B022 to two names, which I think is the worse trade. If the committee later wants two parts, CAR-T is the one I would argue for, ahead of B050.

responses.point: Sten says Nobel practice rarely offers a second chance, so excluding Knudsen is a real cost that the committee should not treat as costless.
responses.response: I agree, and I do not wish to soften it by suggesting she can be recognised later. My answer is different from yours only on what to do about it. Within three names, adding her means removing Drucker, Holst or Mojsov, and each of them has a discovery-level claim that she does not make in the same sense. Her contribution is the engineering of durable drugs. I would put the cost on the record and tie the citation to the physiology and to the principle it established, so that the wording does not claim to honour the drugs.

responses.point: Abdel says B003 would be his fallback if the priority record on GLP-1 were judged too unsettled, and that the UPR's medical impact is indirect.
responses.response: I do not read the priority record on GLP-1 as bad enough to switch, for the reason I give to Svenningsson. If it were, I would want the substitute to be a candidate with clinical effect, and I agree B003 fits that better than B050. I share your concern that any CAR-T citation leaves out the early chimeric-receptor work. That weakens B003 as a replacement for B022, because a fallback ought to be safer on attribution than the candidate it replaces, and here it is not.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active peptide will withstand a careful check of the record, and whether Habener's role requires a different configuration. I have not verified this and cannot do so from the material allowed at this stage.
Whether a citation centred on physiology, with no drug-development laureate, will be read as adequate given that the clinical effect carries much of the case.
Whether the missing early chimeric-receptor work is a fatal gap for B003, which affects how strong an alternative it is.
The concerns raised about a TOR candidate cannot be assessed from the file, so I have not used them in my judgment of B006.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I co-authored nuclear-receptor work with Ronald Evans, who is not on the shortlist, and I have co-authored publications with Per Svenningsson and Abdel El Manira. None involves a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and I do not consider any of it a recusal issue. I have no knowledge of confidential information about the TOR concerns mentioned in round 1.
